description: The multiscale (2nd- and 3rd-order) metallic metamaterial paper: hollow-tube Ni-P hierarchical lattices spanning seven orders of magnitude in feature size, with measured strength-density scaling as low as 1.3 at relative densities below 10^-3, specific tensile strength to 40.8 MPa/(g/cm3) and tensile strains approaching 20%. One of the three measured demonstrations that the hierarchy exponent gain is real. LLNL accepted-manuscript version, LLNL-JRNL-677190.
publisher: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL-JRNL-677190); published as Nature Materials 15(10), 1100-1106 (2016)
licence: DOE public-access accepted manuscript. OSTI record 1458708 lists availability 'External Audience (Unlimited)', journal_type AM, under DOE contract DE-AC52-07NA27344. The Nature Materials version of record remains the publisher's; this stored file is the DOE-released manuscript, not the journal PDF.
attribution: Zheng, X., Smith, W., Jackson, J., Moran, B., Cui, H., Chen, D., Ye, J., Fang, N., Rodriguez, N., Weisgraber, T., and Spadaccini, C. M., 'Multiscale metallic metamaterials', Nature Materials 15(10), 1100-1106 (2016), doi:10.1038/nmat4694. OSTI 1458708, LLNL-JRNL-677190.
